# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .darkfactory/github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## One source per kind of knowledge

### Decision

Four kinds of individually reviewable Markdown source records drive the four human-facing generated documents:

| Source records | Eligible status | Generated artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.darkfactory/agents/notes/*.md` | `published` | `.agents/README.md` |
| `.darkfactory/agents/requests/*.md` | `approved` | `.agents/PRD.md` |
| `.darkfactory/agents/decisions/*.md` | `accepted` | `.agents/ARCHITECTURE.md` |
| `.darkfactory/agents/rules/*.md` | `active` | `.agents/AGENTS.md` |

All selected records require YAML-style front matter containing `status`. Unpublished notes do not contribute to README; `.darkfactory/agents/TODO.md` is a separate, non-generated task file. Other source directories reject files without status rather than silently hiding them. Records assemble in lexical filename order with source backlinks relative to the generated document.

Derived Markdown is committed for review and GitHub rendering, but is not edited independently. A dependency-free Python generator writes it deterministically, and an explicit verification command rejects stale outputs; GitHub CI depends on whether GitHub recognizes the `.github` symlink. Root `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` are Git symlinks to `.agents/README.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.md` respectively.

### Rationale

Separating the public project overview from normative requirements prevents the README from becoming an accidental competing PRD. Flat source folders avoid unnecessary nesting; clear ownership eliminates duplicated content and stale symlinks.

### Consequences

Edit records and regenerate the derived documents in the same change. Draft, rejected and superseded records remain in history but do not appear as current specifications. Public notes are not authoritative product requirements; requirements are owned by requests.

_Source: [0001-single-document-source.md](decisions/0001-single-document-source.md)_


## Development integration and release

### Decision

The `development` branch is the integration branch; `main` is the release branch. Feature work targets `development`. A merge into `main` must originate from `development` and pass required checks and review. Release versions use the root `VERSION` file as their sole source.

Where workflow discovery has been verified, a same-repository pull request receives one version-bump commit on its head branch and a distinct `v<version>` tag and GitHub Release for the merged `main` commit. Existing tags must never be moved. A symlinked `.github` root is **not evidence** that GitHub Actions recognizes workflows; if discovery fails, CI, PR version bump, development branch restoration and automated releases are blocked. A maintainer must verify the change and choose an explicitly approved GitHub-supported activation path before relying on these features.

### Rationale

Separate integration and release lanes prevent ordinary feature PRs from directly entering the release branch. Version commits in the PR branch keep the chosen release number reviewable; tagging on `main` avoids releasing unmerged code.

### Consequences

GitHub branch protection must be configured in repository settings to make workflow checks genuinely mandatory. The workflow source-branch guard is an additional check, not a replacement for protection. Fork pull requests cannot receive automatic head-branch commits with the repository token, and must update their version manually.

_Source: [0002-development-and-release.md](decisions/0002-development-and-release.md)_


## Agent roles and portable skills

### Decision

`.agents/agents/` contains lightweight role profiles (orchestrator, planner, implementer, reviewer and verifier), one Markdown document per role. A role describes authority, inputs, expected output and the handoff; it does not clone global rules.

`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` contains reusable, task-triggered procedures with standard `name` and `description` front matter. Skills cover repository orientation, requirements, architectural decisions, implementation verification, independent review, documentation generation and release checks.

All roles inherit the binding constraints of generated `.agents/AGENTS.md`. Host runtimes may consume these files directly or map them into their own agent/skill registries; placing them here does not imply that a specific runner automatically loads them.

### Rationale

Separating roles from procedures enables composition and provider portability. A planner can use the requirements and architecture skills; a verifier can run implementation and release checks without sharing an implementer's incentives.

### Consequences

A project may add or remove roles and skills based on actual needs. Keep them small, verifiable and grounded in the repository; do not add speculative personalities, redundant rule copies or vendor-specific tooling requirements.

_Source: [0003-agent-roles-and-skills.md](decisions/0003-agent-roles-and-skills.md)_


## Single DarkFactory working tree and test ownership

### Decision

All repository coordination assets live under the physical `.darkfactory/` root:

- `.darkfactory/agents/` owns project requirements, decisions, rules, role profiles, skills, notes and generated documentation.
- `.darkfactory/github/` owns GitHub pull-request templates, workflows and administration scripts.
- `.darkfactory/tests/` is the **only** place to store tests of any type, including unit, integration, functional, smoke, end-to-end, snapshot tests, mocks, fixtures and test helpers.
- Root `.agents` and `.github` must be Git symlinks to `.darkfactory/agents` and `.darkfactory/github` respectively. Root `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` continue to reference the `.agents` alias.

No duplicate copies, test directories outside `.darkfactory/tests/`, or separate actual `.agents` / `.github` trees are allowed. The generator enforces symlink targets and audits tracked test locations.

### Trade-off and activation boundary

GitHub expects executable workflow files physically discoverable under root `.github/workflows/`. GitHub Actions has not established reliable support for a symlinked root `.github` directory. This structural decision prioritizes a canonical `.darkfactory` tree; workflow definitions under `.darkfactory/github/workflows/` **must not be claimed as active** until live event triggers prove discovery. No workflow, version-bump, branch-source policy or release action should be marked operational based only on the files' presence.

Restoring GitHub-native automation requires a separately approved, GitHub-supported activation arrangement. Do not silently reverse the symlink requirement or manufacture passing CI results.

### Consequences

Tooling resolves its workspace by the physical location of `.darkfactory/`, while conventional root aliases remain available to humans and local tools. Tests run from `.darkfactory/tests/`; test code elsewhere is a repository-layout violation.

_Source: [0004-single-darkfactory-root.md](decisions/0004-single-darkfactory-root.md)_
